newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong, CKI shares remain strong.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong, CKI shares remain strong.

text.p: Shares of Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) remained firm on Wednesday morning following Tuesday's surge on the reorganisation of the Cheung Kong group.
Cheung Kong shares were up HK$1.75 to HK$74.50 in late morning and CKI edged up HK$0.30 to HK$21.55.
"Anticipation of stronger and better earnings growth of the group following the restructuring continued to give investors an excuse to buy," said a sales manager at a local brokerage.

Analysts said anticipation that Cheung Kong will recieve an exceptional gain from the deal and at the same time get a majority stake in Hutchison Whampoa Ltd had given investors confidence in the group's future.
But Hutchison and Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd shares tended weaker, with Hutchison flat at HK$61.25 and Hongkong Electric HK$0.55 lower at HK$27.10.
Hutchison plans to make a general offer for Hongkong Electric at HK$26.50 a share and then transfer a controlling stake in the utility to CKI in exchange for new CKI shares.

"The (downward) adjustment (in Hongkong Electric) is reasonable in view of a limited upside potential following their recent gain, and an offer price of HK$26.50 for each Hongkong Electric share," said Michael Ng from Sassoon Securities.
Cheung Kong will also transfer its existing shareholding of 70.66 percent in CKI to Hutchison for about HK$20.45 billion.
Brokers said the recent strong flat sales response also underpined demand for the property counters.
Brokers said they expected the Cheung Kong group of companies to remain firm in the short run.
